title: Fetch and Carry: A Mission From a Shelf to a Table, With the Rule That the Base Moves Only When the Arm Is Tucked and the Arm Moves Only When the Base Is Still

questions.question: Why must the base not drive with the arm out?
options: The arm's joints overheat while the base is moving
It tips (33-05) and the hand is hard to control
The camera on the hand cannot see the route
The wheels slip under the extra weight
questions.explanation: With the arm out the centre of mass is forward and the tipping limit is lower, and every bump of the base swings the hand.

questions.question: A mission that went to plan took:
options: 113 ticks
97 ticks
100 ticks
15 ticks
questions.explanation: 97 ticks with nothing going wrong. One missed grasp and a retry brought it to 113.

questions.question: A battery of 4.5 Wh for a mission needing 4.0 Wh:
options: Started, and stopped in fault 4 half way
Ran to the end with nothing to spare
Stopped at the start, in fault 4
Was allowed, since 4.5 is more than 4.0
questions.explanation: The mission needs 1.2 times its energy before it starts, 4.8 Wh here. Refusing at the start is better than stopping half way to the table.

questions.question: The faulty plan with the interlock had how many unsafe ticks?
questions.explanation: The interlock held the base whenever the arm was out, so the faulty plan never moved unsafely. Without it the same plan drove with the arm out for 15 ticks.

questions.question: What did the interlock turn the bug into?
options: A mission that finished late
A robot that drove slowly with the arm out
A stopped robot (a timeout)
A fault 1, no part
questions.explanation: The base was never allowed to drive, the step ran out of time, and the mission ended in fault 3. Nothing moved that should not have.

questions.question: Why is the interlock separate from the state machine?
options: So that it can be switched off for testing
Because the state machine has no room for more states
So that it runs on the arm's controller
It holds even when the state machine is wrong
questions.explanation: The state machine is long and can have a bug, as the plan that skipped the stow did. The rule is two lines applied to every command, whatever asked for it.
